instructions: Python CLI (src/, scripts/, tests/) plus the WGS Extract desktop app under gui/: a TypeScript Node backend and browser Web UI packaged with Tauri (Rust) for Windows, macOS and Linux. Skip style/formatting nits (ruff handles Python). Focus on correctness, security, cross-platform behavior and maintainability.

rules.rule: Avoid bare `except:` and overly broad `except Exception:`. Catch specific exception types.
Configuration display, logs, and error messages must redact keys, tokens, and credentials.

Use pathlib.Path for filesystem path operations; do not introduce os.path calls. Shared path helpers accept str | os.PathLike[str]. Keep Path values while manipulating paths and convert explicitly at string-based CLI, configuration, subprocess-wrapper, and public return-value boundaries. Preserve known compound genomic extensions with input_stem/fasta_prefix and append index sidecars with append_suffix, not with_suffix. Tool wrapper commands and samtools out##idx##index arguments are strings, not filesystem paths. Use native path strings except for portable checksum-manifest entries.
Public functions and methods should have type annotations on parameters and return values.
The Tauri shell hosts the window, menus, native pickers, and updater. Bundle loading, setup, and action logic belong in the TypeScript server. Flag misplaced logic.
Configuration display must redact keys, tokens, and secrets. Flag any code path that prints or logs raw credential-shaped values.
Code in gui/app/shared must run in both Node and the browser. Disallow Node-only APIs (fs, path, process, child_process, os); those belong in gui/app/web/src/server only.
The Web UI is TypeScript compiled by tsc to vanilla ES modules with no bundler/framework. Flag introductions of bundlers, frameworks, or heavy runtime dependencies.
Every interactive control needs an accessible label (label/aria-label/title). Prefer semantic HTML over div soup.
Code must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Flag hard-coded path separators, POSIX-only shell commands, or platform assumptions without a platform branch.
